title: Globex Quarterly Business Review
overview: Globex adoption reached 84% weekly active across 150 seats, up from 61% last quarter.
Managers save about 5 hours a week; automatic action items are the most-loved feature.
Pain points: transcript accuracy for strong accents and speaker identification in shared conference rooms.
Requests: custom vocabulary and a Zendesk integration that attaches call summaries to tickets.
The contract renews in February with a planned 50-seat expansion, which depends on SSO shipping this quarter.

comments.body: SSO is the gating item for both Globex and Northwind. Flagging this to Marcus.

transcript: Emily Watson: Hi Grace, welcome to the quarterly business review. I'll walk through adoption and impact, then I'd love to hear your feedback, and we'll finish with the roadmap and renewal.
Grace Liu: Sounds great. I've got about thirty minutes.
Emily Watson: Let's start with adoption. You have one hundred and fifty seats, and eighty four percent of them were weekly active last quarter. That's up from sixty one percent the quarter before.
Grace Liu: That's good to see. The support managers especially use it every day for escalation calls.
Emily Watson: On impact, your managers told us they save about five hours a week on note taking and follow ups. Across the team that's roughly the equivalent of three full time people.
Grace Liu: That's consistent with what I hear. The automatic action items are the favorite feature. Nobody has to chase who promised what after a call.
Daniel Okafor: That's great to hear. Are there areas where it's not working as well?
Grace Liu: Yes, two things. First, transcript accuracy for some of our agents with strong accents is noticeably worse. Our team in Manila sees more errors than the team in Dublin.
Grace Liu: Second, speaker identification gets confused when several people join from the same conference room.

Jordan Rivera: Thanks, that's really useful. On accents, we're rolling out a new speech model next month that was trained on a much more diverse dataset. Early tests show about thirty percent fewer errors for non native speakers.
Jordan Rivera: For conference rooms, the fix is harder. One option is a custom vocabulary plus manual speaker labels that the model learns from over time.
Grace Liu: Custom vocabulary would help a lot anyway. Our product names get transcribed wrong all the time.
Emily Watson: I'll set you up for the early access program for the new speech model, so your Manila team can try it first.
Grace Liu: Perfect. The other big request is a Zendesk integration. Our support tickets live in Zendesk, and agents want call summaries attached to the ticket automatically.
Jordan Rivera: That's been requested by a few support teams. It's not on the Q4 roadmap, but I'll take it back to the team and come back with a timeline.
Grace Liu: Even a rough timeline would help me plan.
Daniel Okafor: Let's talk about the renewal. Your contract renews in February. Based on the adoption, are you thinking about expanding?
Grace Liu: Yes. Our customer success team wants fifty more seats. The blocker for them is SSO, our security team won't approve more users without it.
Daniel Okafor: SSO with SAML is shipping this quarter, so the timing works well for a February renewal.
Grace Liu: Then I'd like a renewal proposal that includes the extra fifty seats, and ideally a multi year option.
Daniel Okafor: I'll prepare a proposal with one year and two year options, including the expansion, and send it by the end of next week.
Emily Watson: I'd also suggest a short training session for the customer success team before they're onboarded, to get adoption high from day one.
Grace Liu: Yes, please. A forty five minute session would be ideal. Let's also add our VP of Support as an executive sponsor, she's been asking about ROI.
Emily Watson: Great, I'll send an ROI summary she can share internally, based on the time savings we discussed.
Grace Liu: Perfect. This was a productive review. Thank you all.
Emily Watson: Thanks Grace. I'll send a recap with all of the next steps today.
